solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shake leg that's slipped on rug

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee

indicators.note: something slipped is out of place, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shakes a leg and slips on a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is the slang sense of a toupee, not a floor covering; 'slipped' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for moving with small rapid jerky motions, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Feminine ambition gripping the country

indicators.note: gripping means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: a wish is a desire or ambition
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A feminine ambition has taken hold of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' is the container signal: the ambition holds the country, an Arabian sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: It means like a woman, typically used of a man, so it is a near synonym.

clue.text: Point of fork stuck up into melon, as bits tucked away?

indicators.note: into puts these letters inside the other word

parts.note: Galia is a variety of melon

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read backwards

parts.note: a tine is a prong of a fork

explanation.surface: A fork prong jabbed into a melon, its bits hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' reverses TINE to ENIT, which goes 'into' GALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Private parts are bits normally kept covered, a jokey description of the sexual organs.

clue.text: Heavy metal front man?

definitions.meaning: a dense soft grey metal, symbol Pb
the one at the front, as a band's singer or a ... actor

explanation.surface: The front man of a heavy metal band.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a dense metal, and the role of the person who goes first or stars.

clue.text: Brown cat with loose skin, for real

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
a gib is a male cat, especially a castrated one

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outer layer, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Description of a brown cat with loose skin, offered as genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' takes the outside letters of 'loose', L and E. GIB, a tomcat, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangible can be touched, so it is actual and concrete, not imagined.

clue.text: One retaliating, losing rag even?

indicators.note: losing suggests the letters are lost from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone getting their own back by losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing rag' reads as losing one's temper, British slang, but 'losing' rearranges RAG EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes revenge is someone hitting back for a wrong.

clue.text: Fit on heads of Boy Scouts, hat that's sweet

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a fit is a bout or spell, as is a go

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of the words

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Fitting hats on Boy Scouts' heads.
explanation.walkthrough: A large hard round sweet, a British boiled confection that lasts a long time in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a kind of hard sweet, so the definition names its category.

clue.text: Head cold in skull, perhaps?

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word

parts.note: a skull is an example of a bone

explanation.surface: A head cold felt in the skull.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for the skull or noggin, so a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Self-seeker, say, is found in the Bible

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means

indicators.note: found in puts these letters inside the other piece

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A selfish person, for example, appears in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; 'the Bible' is narrowed to its first part, the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selfish, always seeking personal advantage, so the terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Classes in Shakespeare neglected, upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Classes in which Shakespeare is ignored, to someone's dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run 'shakespeARE NEGlected'; 'upset' turns it up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology these are taxonomic groups, so they are categories or classes.

clue.text: Element having unusual name, gas describing neon

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw round, so these letters go around the neon symbol
unusual signals that these letters come out in a different arrangement

parts.note: NE is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: an element with an odd name, a gas that describes neon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' gives MANGASE; 'describing' works in its geometry sense, drawing a line round neon's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a chemical element, the metal with atomic number 25.

clue.text: Dispose of green light for house

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
a green light means go

explanation.surface: An instruction to get rid of the green light in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, house (or housey-housey) is an old name for the numbers game played in halls.
explanation.definitionFit: House is an old British name for the same numbers-and-cards game, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Screwy fasteners?

definitions.meaning: small threaded metal pieces that go on bolts; the question mark nods at screws

explanation.surface: Fasteners that are oddly crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: slang for mad, and the threaded blocks screwed onto bolts.

clue.text: Number among twelve evenly distributed on ship, floating

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece placed on another follows it
among means set in the middle of the other letters
evenly picks the letters in even positions of the word, second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: eight is a number
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A number among twelve items spread evenly over a ship that is afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly distributed' takes W, L, E from 'twelve'; 'among' puts EIGHT among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floating free, as in space, has no felt weight.

clue.text: Unknown quantity buried by labrador after chewing on end of bone that's sharp

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on another sits above it
buried by means held inside the other letters
chewing mangles the letters into a new order

parts.note: Z is an unknown in algebra

indicators.note: the end is the last letter

explanation.surface: A dog buries something after chewing on the end of a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after chewing' scrambles LABRADOR to RAORBLAD; 'buried by' puts Z inside; E, 'end of bone', goes under.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaving edge is a sharp item, described here as the thing that is keen.

clue.text: A shrivelled up concubine?

parts.note: a dried grape, also read jokily as a sultan's wife or consort past her prime

explanation.surface: A wizened woman of the harem.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a dried seedless grape and the wife or consort of a sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is literally shrivelled, and the same word names a sultan's consort.

clue.text: Statement on the left

parts.note: re means on, concerning
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A political statement on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the left' is not politics but the port side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an account given of something, as in a news piece.

clue.text: Sheridan plays about old African once

indicators.note: about means going around the other letter
plays signals the letters move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Plays by Sheridan about an old African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges SHERIDAN; 'about' puts O inside. Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an 18th-century playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe, so a native of it was an African of a now vanished state.

clue.text: Group of islands offering rival deal in uprising

parts.note: anti means opposing, as a rival does

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sell is to deal in goods

explanation.surface: Islands offering a competing trade deal during a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in uprising' turns SELL to LLES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antilles are a Caribbean island chain, so the term names a group of islands.

clue.text: Sound of explosion, a shocker in outskirts of Khartoum

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the others
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters

parts.note: boo is what you shout to give someone a shock

explanation.surface: A blast heard on the edge of Khartoum, a shocking event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of Khartoum' gives K and M, with A BOO set between them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a comic-book word imitating a loud blast, so it is a word for that noise.

clue.text: Drink, having little eating skill

indicators.note: eating means taking the other letters inside

parts.note: mini means little
art is a skill

explanation.surface: Having a drink, with a little skill in eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' is the container signal: the small word swallows the skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of gin and vermouth, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Secure passport stamped with initial of evacuee, entering urban area

indicators.note: entering puts these letters inside the others

parts.note: a town is an urban area

indicators.note: a passport stamped with something has it put on, here inside it

parts.note: a passport is a form of ID

indicators.note: the initial is the first letter

explanation.surface: An evacuee's passport is stamped on entering a town, keeping them safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'stamped with' puts the evacuee's initial into the passport, giving IED, and 'entering' sends that into the town.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down a load is to fasten it, making it secure.

clue.text: Company relocating to Peru

indicators.note: relocating moves the letters to new places

explanation.surface: A firm moving its base to Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' suggests a business, but means a band of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre company of actors or dancers is a touring band of performers.

clue.text: Many notches

definitions.meaning: cuts or marks, as on a tally stick

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: lots of something, and cuts made as marks, from tally notches counted in twenties.

clue.text: Two taps on orange sink, something to go on

parts.note: taps are marked C and H, cold and hot
amber is an orange-yellow colour
to sink a ball in snooker is to pot it

explanation.surface: A kitchen or bathroom fitting: two taps on an orange sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' is not the basin but a snooker verb. 'go' is a euphemism for using the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom pot for night use is literally a receptacle to relieve oneself in, the euphemistic sense of go.

clue.text: A story about a formation of flying geese is quick

indicators.note: about means going around the letter

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
geese fly in a V-shaped formation

explanation.surface: A tale about geese flying in formation, told quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' is in the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick meant living in old English, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Sound Indian location for shop

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard, not written, here sounding like an Indian city

parts.note: Delhi is a city in India

explanation.surface: A sound Indian spot for a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (reliable) but signals a homophone; the H of Delhi is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for delicatessen, a shop selling cooked meats and prepared food.

clue.text: Bend to cut top from tree

indicators.note: cutting the top removes its first letter

parts.note: a larch is a conifer tree

explanation.surface: Bending down to trim the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut top from' removes L from LARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to curve or bow, as a cat does its back.

clue.text: Condiment from Agra, I take?

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone takes a condiment from the city of Agra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points inside 'agRA I TAke'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber, eaten as an accompaniment.

clue.text: Neutral island, military seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means holding these letters inside

parts.note: martial means military
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A neutral island where the military seizes power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' puts P inside MARTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: taking no side, unbiased.

clue.text: Remove villainous vixen

parts.note: to shed is to remove or cast off
evil means villainous

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a wicked female fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vixen' is not the fox but a spiteful, bad-tempered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A vixen is also a fierce, malicious woman, which is what this hyphenated term means.

clue.text: Cheers, seeing back of fish in aquaria

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other word

parts.note: aquaria are fish tanks

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A toast, seeing the tail of a fish in the aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of fish' gives H, put inside TANKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for an expression of gratitude, so they are synonyms.
